result.title: CapLite: Prompt-Injection Defense for Small Language Model Agents without Model-Written Security Artifacts
result.summary: Enforcement defenses against prompt injection, such as CaMeL, Progent, IPIGuard and DRIFT, ask the agent's own model to write a security artifact (a program, a privilege policy, a dependency graph or a constraint list) that code then enforces. We ask whether small language model (SLM) agents can be trusted to write these artifacts. Across 15 open-weight models, 13 of them between 1.7B and 12B parameters, they cannot: the policies, graphs and constraints that the agent's model writes admit attacks on 14 (Progent), 13 (IPIGuard) and 11 (DRIFT) of the models, and CaMeL's programs fail to run in up to 68% of episodes. We present CapLite, which derives its policy from the tool schemas, commits the write calls before any tool result is read, and admits a write only if every argument that decides whom or what it affects is stated in the user's request. This guarantees write integrity: injected text cannot add a write, and no write reaches a recipient, amount, object or destination that the user did not state. No attack succeeds in 13,935 attacked AgentDojo episodes. CapLite reaches utility under attack comparable to CaMeL's (29.0% vs. 27.2%) with fewer tokens than every other enforcement defense and than the undefended agent: 17.1k per episode, 18% of CaMeL's, and the highest utility per token of all enforcement defenses.

AI.brief_summary: 论文检验 15 个开源小模型能否可信地自写安全伪影（策略、依赖图、约束表），发现多数模型的产物可被注入攻破，转而提出 CapLite：从工具 schema 派生策略，在读取任何工具结果前提交写调用，且仅当决定「影响谁/什么」的每个参数都由用户请求明示时才允许写入，在 AgentDojo 的攻击回合中零成功并显著降低 token 成本。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「不信任模型自写的中间约束、改用 schema 派生的外部可核验契约」以及「先提交再读取证据」的思路，可能可供核查 LVR 中 latent/内部状态的可信度、信息坍缩与何时允许摄取新证据（LOOK/STOP）的问题，但本文属智能体安全领域，与视觉推理无直接联系，需较多迁移判断。
